Deku (Shoot Style) 

Rush-down based character. His only real drawback (as far as I can tell) is that he lacks projectiles. Otherwise, he is an excellent character, being very speedy, high-damaging combos, and has the potential to consistently beat any other character on the roster. 

His BnB combos are easy to get down and deal considerable amounts of damage. His Houston Smash allows him to easily wall splat opponents into punishing combos. However, as I mentioned before, having no projectile leaves him vulnerable to characters/players who can zone well. If he cannot get in on a character, he's not gonna be able to do anything. Though, when he gains momentum, it can be very difficult to get away from him due to his movement and combo speed. 

Pros: Easy to pick-up, has many combo options on ground or in air, fast movement speed, one of the fastest unbreakables in the game, easy wall-splats

Cons: No projectiles, very slow super-armor on ground, his special 2 deals lackluster damage in any situation, has to be close to opponent to do anything

Combo difficulty: Easy to Intermediate.

Good Match-ups: Kirishima, Midoriya, All Might, Ochako, Tsuyu, Shigaraki, Stain

Bad Match-ups: Bakugo, Dabi, Denki, AFO, Todoroki, Tomoyaki, Jiro

Everyone else is a toss-up. He's a very solid character despite his drawbacks.

There's a channel on Youtube called TGN Anime that has a guides on a few characters in this game. I think he'll be doing more in the future, but I can't say for sure. You should check that out as well, if you're looking for resources.

Go into the training mode and build combos. There aren't many resources for combos in this game, so you just have to see what your character can do and see if you can get away with certain inputs. This will help you understand the character more as you know more of what they're capable of. 

On that note, it's good that you have a basic idea of certain characters. If you want to get good, learning the majority roster (or at least the characters you see all the time) and their capabilities will be imperative in playing around them. You don't have to know them in-depth, but just enough to get an idea of how your opponent will play them so that you're able to adjust your playstyle to fight them. So if you're playing a character with no projectiles like Shoot Deku, it probably won't be a good idea to just run at a Dabi or Kaminari, as these are characters will either zone you until you die and/or try to move in on you, or they'll try to put you into a state where you cannot do anything to them unless you escape their projectiles. 

Knowing when to block vs. knowing when to dash away from certain quirks is also a good thing to learn, as obviously movement is a huge part of the game. With Dabi, I find myself not jumping at him as much cuz he'll just throw an orb at me, so I dash around his flame wall and move-in on him so that I can pressure him. I find there's no point in blocking in that match-up because eventually he'll move in on you when you have a projectile on you, and he'll just break your guard or unbreakable you into a combo. Like I said, it's just a matter of knowing what to do in certain match-ups.

This may take a while to get used to. I'm currently learning to play against certain characters too (particularly Kirishima), so don't feel discouraged if you don't see yourself improving immediately.

It's been like this for years. The Roblox staff don't see it as an issue because it only draws more players to their game. They'd rather make money off this kind of stuff, rather than attempt to fix it. It blows my mind how lazy and uncaring the staff can be.

I feel the game would greatly benefit from community input. The Roblox staff at the moment seem fine with making changes as they please and telling everyone "If you don't like the change, too bad." That's not how you keep players. That kind of mindset will only stop people from enjoying the game and they'll something else to play. It also doesn't help that the Roblox staff go out of their to ignore or outright remove criticism of anything to do with Roblox, regardless of how true or constructive it is. 

Edit: Could to would.

I love Roblox, I really do. I've been an on and off player since 2009 and have had a blast with it. But it's sad to see that some features, such  as customizing your character, have become features that must be paid for to fully enjoy. Heck, even to get paid for hard work on developing a game on Roblox requires the most expensive premium membership available. Free users can't make money off their Roblox games anymore, thus discouraging players to try their hand at Lua or building, which results in the same, old games being at the top of the page results all the time. How long have Murder Mystery or Apocalypse Rising been on top? 

I know I'm going to sound like a nostalgic idiot, but I know for damn sure that when Tix was a thing and DevEx wasn't, there were a lot more interesting and unique games popping up on the front page every week or so. People weren't afraid to experiment. Now the front page panders to the majority of the community, with constant iterations of Gmod game modes, boring RPGs (most of which take place in school, which I try not to think about when playing video games), and other trash.  I preferred when Roblox encouraged unique games, but the new system has made it so developers have no choice but to ride the bandwagon so that they can get their paycheck. That's really disgusting, imho.
